policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the connective as causal 'for fornicators and adulterers God will judge', which answers to gar; the RP adversative de would have given ASV's usual 'but'.

Aorist subjunctive enkatalipo and present enkataleipo are rendered alike by 'neither will I in any wise forsake thee'; no ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes them, so the SBLGNT base fallback carries the projection.

ASV joins the two clauses of the Ps. 118:6 quotation with a semicolon ('is my helper; I will not fear'), and an untranslated kai in quoted poetry is ordinary ASV practice; the absence of 'and' is not a positive distinction, so both readings stand.

'they that occupied themselves', with the note 'Greek walked', reflects the participle's lexeme but not its tense; present peripatountes and aorist peripatesantes are indistinguishable in this rendering.
ASV prints 'Through him then let us offer up', and its textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities omit then' marks the omission as the variant; the text therefore reads oun.

'we are persuaded' is ASV's rendering of the present passive peithometha; the perfect pepoithamen is elsewhere rendered 'we trust' / 'we are confident' (so KJV here, following the RP reading), and ASV's departure from it marks the present.
ASV reads 'in every good thing' with no noun for ergo, and its textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read work' relegates the added ergo to the margin.
ASV text has 'working in us', rendering hemin, while its textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read you' marks hymin as the marginal reading.
ASV's 'for ever and ever' is glossed 'Greek unto the ages of the ages', which quotes the underlying text as eis tous aionas ton aionon and so attests the added ton aionon.
ASV reads 'our brother Timothy', supplying the possessive that renders hemon; the RP omission would leave 'the brother Timothy'.
ASV prints 'Grace be with you all. Amen.' with no note marking Amen as doubtful, rendering the added amen.
